title: Stratified hit-rate ensemble for KV prefix TTL tuning and safe rollback
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description:
Objective: produce an automated recommendation engine that suggests per-prefix TTLs and cache-key shaping rules informed by a stratified ensemble of hit-rate models, explicitly accounting for request batching behavior, and a deterministic safe-apply + rollback runbook for production rollout.

Background: Prefix-level caching has large cost leverage but brittle when popularity shifts or when batch scheduling changes per-token compute. Existing heuristics produce conservative TTLs that leave cost on the table. This work builds a multi-model pipeline that: (1) stratifies prefixes by traffic shape (burstiness, session-locality, sequence-length correlation), (2) trains lightweight hit-rate predictors per-stratum (time-series + Bayesian smoothing + a simple tree-based model), (3) ensembles predictions with an uncertainty quantifier to generate a recommended TTL range and confidence band, and (4) outputs concrete cache key shaping suggestions (collapse low-entropy suffixes, preserve conversational session tokens, avoid user-id leakage).

Safety & rollout: recommendations are subject to a four-stage apply protocol: dry-run shadow replay (no production cache writes), staged canary with traffic-sliced prefixes (1% -> 5% -> 25%), automated metrics gate at each step, and full rollout. Gates include: rolling-average hit-rate delta threshold (no >5% relative drop in any stratum), tail latency SLO delta (p95 increase <10ms), token-cost reduction floor (>1% expected), and user-facing error rate (no regressions). If a gate fails, an automatic staged rollback is executed with preserved pre-change mappings. All applies require an immutable audit artifact linking the recommendation payload, model version, and simulation run ID.

Technical plan: implement a simulator that consumes sampled request traces (stratified by tenant, model, route) to compute counterfactual hit-rate / cost / latency for candidate TTLs and key transforms. Produce a single recommendation JSON per rollout containing: recommended TTL, confidence band, expected cost delta, per-stratum risk score, and rollback criteria. Integrate with existing rollout orchestration (ENG-204801) and the canary harness (ENG-995713).

Metrics to monitor: per-prefix hit-rate, per-stratum latency (p50/p95), cache write/write-failure rate, KV lookup QPS, token cost per 1k requests, and model uncertainty score. Add synthetic probes for prefixes with very low volume to avoid noisy decisions.

Acceptance criteria: (a) simulator reproduces historical hit-rates within +/-3% for test traces, (b) ensemble recommendations yield >=3% net token-cost reduction in small-scale canary without violating latency SLOs, (c) full runbook tested in staging with automated rollback triggers, (d) docs and runbook published and reviewed by reliability and security teams.
